slice.name: restart_journal_index_reconstruction_duplicate_replay
slice.purpose: Simulate process restart after accepted e4b, discard the ephemeral applied-event registry, reconstruct the e4b idempotency entry solely by validating and scanning its durable complete framed-journal record, then replay the identical frame and verify zero second effect.

journal_reconstruction.canonicalization: UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted keys and separators ',' ':'; complete frame has one trailing newline.

slice.tested_scope: Deterministic small text state; one already accepted e4b complete frame; one simulated process restart; reconstruction of the relevant e4b idempotency entry from that validated durable frame; and one immediate identical-frame replay after restart. This demonstrates that the idempotency fact needed for this replay need not reside only in ephemeral memory. It does not prove reconstruction of an arbitrarily long/corrupted journal, delayed duplicates after intervening accepted events, compaction/tombstone behavior, lock-free progress, fairness, semantic model-weight adaptation, or indefinite repository availability.

zero_dependency_assessment.transport_note: All digest validation, journal-index reconstruction, restart simulation and replay logic were deterministic Chat-local computation. Repository contents API served only as lightweight durable transport; no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package storage, cloud credit, external model/API credit, richer execution mode, protected authority, manual user execution, scheduler mutation or incremental monetary cost was required.

slice.conflict_check: Only current sanitized controls, own role-local clean state and Chat-local computation were used. No O/O-derived, downstream, other-worker, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config or legacy semantic input was consumed; no protected-primary or scheduler mutation occurred.
